thesis: John Chambers argues that a company must undergo a near-death experience to transition from being good to becoming great, a lesson he learned from Jack Welch after the 2001 recession. He explains that this crisis forces leaders to question their ability to lead and motivates them to develop stronger leadership skills than they would have in good times.
